title: How a Garage Door Opener Works in 60 Seconds 🚗⚙️ #shorts
description:
A garage door can weigh hundreds of pounds, yet a small motor lifts it every day. Big springs carry almost all the weight, while a motor pulls a trolley along a rail to guide the door. Rolling codes keep the remote secure, and an invisible beam near the floor stops the door from closing on anything. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#garagedoor #smarthome #howitworks
tags: how a garage door opener works

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: A garage door can weigh *hundreds of pounds*. The opener barely lifts any of it.

steps.label: Springs
steps.text: Tight *torsion springs* above the door twist and pull cables that carry *almost all* its weight.

steps.label: Motor
steps.text: A *motor* and reduction gears drive a *chain* or belt along a rail on the ceiling.

steps.label: Trolley
steps.text: The chain pulls a *trolley*, and an arm drags the door *up* or down its tracks.

steps.label: Remote
steps.text: Your remote sends a *rolling code*. Each code works only once, so a copied one is useless.

steps.label: Safety
steps.text: An *infrared beam* runs just above the floor. Break it, and the door *reverses*.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Springs lift, motor *guides*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
